utterances.speaker: MIOMIR ZUZUL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you mentioned in that record I believe, if I'm not mistaken, around that same time you had involvements with Mr. Komsic that in fact you reported, I think that's when there were discussions about whether it was completely Mr. Komsic's proposal or not and then conversations with Mr. Redman. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR ZUZUL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I think that I said that Mr. Silajdzic had told me that it was not only Komsic's proposal. I think that that's the way I put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely right. Absolutely correct. Now, if I can ask you to go to Exhibit P 10403. I'm afraid, sir, that I have to put one last book in front of you today, and to the best of my knowledge, Your Honours, I'll tell you this is my last exhibit. Mr. Komsic -- this Mr. Komsic wrote a book and actually it's been listed and used in this case by both the Defence and Prosecution, various excerpts, called: "Surviving a country" by Komsic. And there's a chapter or portion of his book, if you haven't had a chance to read, I guess I have to break the news to you which is titled: "Zuzul's blackmail." And you have Exhibit P 10403, Mr. Komsic is giving an account and in this chapter it starts, in fact on 11th of February, 1994, so two or three days prior to the presidential transcript meeting that we looked at earlier today. He talks about being in Geneva and he talks about Mr. Silajdzic, which seems to be consistent. "Silajdzic insisted that there were no borders between the Muslims and the Croats, the borders were an invention leading to war and that everything was the consequence of Tudjman's obsession with getting the former Banovina. Zuzul reacted and there was a heavy exchange of words. (Granic left yesterday and took our plan to Zagreb). It was not possible to have a proper dialogue after that." Now, if I can direct your attention, please, to the last page of this excerpt, on page 3, the top of the page, please. "The conference increased the tension between the two delegations, the HNV and Herceg-Bosna, both in Geneva." Now, can we agree, sir, that the HNV is a reference to the Croatian National Council, a body that had been formed in Sarajevo and was another organization of Bosnian Croats that you spoke about earlier today; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR ZUZUL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Komsic says that: "Zuzul invited me for a talk about this. It was a very unpleasant and difficult conversation. He first tried to tell me his personal views trying to give me some advice. When this did not help and I stated the arguments that completely justified everything that we had done and proposed, he told me the 'government' position. He was clear and unambiguous, and in addition to mentioning high treason, he threatened me. He warned me that 'they' had my family, who were in Sisak, under control. I told him that I was not impressed by these threats because they had tried to kill me before, my property was confiscated and divided, an arrest warrant was issued for my son and they were threatening me publicly and arrogantly on Croatian Television. I reminded him of the appearance of Ignjac Kostroman on Croatian Radio Television." Do you recall, sir, having this conversation with Mr. Komsic around the 11th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR ZUZUL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation, as is described here, is the sort of conversation I've never had with anyone, including Mr. Komsic. I can't remember and I can't make any claims about meeting up with him or not on that day. I must say that I am scandalised by this. For instance, he said that he left our premises in the United Nations building excited and encouraged. I never had an office in the United Nations building, so to say the least, he is lying about the venue of the meeting. Allow me, Mr. Prosecutor, to put a logical question. Two days after what happened an official record was made. Was there anything in what was recorded as me having said that even remotely resembles what is written by Mr. Komsic here? You have gone over the better part of my career as a diplomat and not only as a diplomat. Did you ever come across a situation where I threatened anyone, mentioned anyone's family, or anything of the sort? Yesterday we had occasion to see the way Mr. Komsic addressed at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I'm not sure that you would have necessarily reported that in the meeting in Zagreb, but perhaps you would have. But be that as it may, sir, let me direct your attention to the next paragraph. "In the end, I told him that they did not have the right to decide about our lives, our property, and our history, and we would not become a national minority in order for a handful of Herzegovinians to have their own state. I left their offices in the UN building, both excited and encouraged. I finally realized that they were powerless. Out of control, Zuzul said at one point, 'You got rid of Boban, but you won't get rid of Tudjman.'" Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR ZUZUL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did not make it. A moment ago in my answer I told you that Mr. Komsic was even lying about the venue of the meeting. What were these offices of ours in the UN building that he was coming out of? We never had anything of the sort. He was lying about the venue and about everything else. Whoever knows me would find it inconceivable -- well, after all, I'm 185 centimetres tall and I have as many kilogrammes as I have, and Mr. Komsic is a rather short, tiny person. Would I threaten him? Nowhere in any of the texts will you find me advocating any sort of an option that he suddenly seems to be claiming that I espoused. These are just fabrications in the service of I do not know whom, but they are not the truth. I have never said anything bad about Mr. Komsic and I was always a minority in behaving thus, and that's why all the more so am I surprised in seeing that he is putting these words into my mouth that do not tally with my personality, with my political views, and this event as described herein never occurred. The same Mr. Komsic, as we had occasion to see in the transcript from the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which I was unaware of until yesterday, makes it his business to invent derogatory terms for his compatriots, Croats, at the Assembly. So that's the sort of man he was, and I was not aware of that until yesterday. Not even now that I know this would I threaten him politically and even less so physically. Your Honours, would I ever include in a threat somebody's family? The family, to my mind, is something sacred, it comes before everything else, and I am really shocked that anybody should wish to impute something of the sort to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Zuzul, I want to thank you for coming to The Hague and giving your testimony and that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas, will we have re-direct tomorrow? Maybe you don't have re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This cross calls for no re-direct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's good news. Nobody had expected that. Witness, on behalf of my fellow Judges I would like to thank you for having come and testified here. It was lengthy but necessary because both the Defence and the Prosecution needed to put questions to you. I wish you and the family members accompanying you a safe trip back home. Could Mr. Usher escort the witness back out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you sent us the schedule for after court recess. I think a witness is scheduled. I don't believe he's been granted protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The next witness, no, Your Honour, and I should note, I should note, that after that witness we're still trying to make arrangements to bring the -- Mr. Perkovic back to follow-up. We're waiting to hear back. As soon as we hear back, we hope within the next day or so, certainly before Friday, we will communicate that news. We do -- Mr. Scott did approach me yesterday and I did give my assurances that as soon as we know we will let everybody know so they could prepare accordingly. So in any event, we might have an updated calendar for all of you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As you well know, we shall re-convene after court recess. We have a few minutes left, but I take this opportunity to wish everyone a good rest. We have spent some three intense months, so I encourage you all to take a good rest. We shall re-convene on Monday, August the 25th, at quarter past 2.00. That's all. I need to leave, because in less than 25 minutes I'll be back in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
